title: field-notes-preemptive-batch-probing
summary: Working notes from exploratory experiments on combining light preemption and small probes to reduce tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants while maintaining throughput and fairness.
background: We operate a continuous batching scheduler with knobs: max_batch_size, timeout_ms, age_boost, preempt_threshold and probe_ratio. Prior runs focused on size/timeouts. These notes explore preemption + probes + tenant-weighted fairness against replayed production traffic with injected microbursts.
key_hypotheses: H1: Moderate preemption targeted at freeing space for high-age requests reduces p99 for latency-sensitive tenants with small throughput cost.
H2: Low-rate 1-2 token probes reduce first-token spikes by warming KV/cache state for models with large KV footprints.
H3: Age-weighted tenant priority avoids starvation and preserves background throughput while benefitting high-priority tails.
testbed: staging-gpu-cluster-3 (4x A100), runtime main@6b2a1f with batching refactor, kernel timing enabled; traffic is 2h slices of prod replay + 10s 500rps microbursts every 120s; tenants: S (sensitive low qps), B (background high qps), P (platform), T (noisy). Warmup 30m, measure 60m.
configs_tested: baseline: max_batch=32 timeout_ms=8 age_boost=1 preempt_thresh=0 probe_ratio=0
A: max_batch=32 timeout_ms=8 age_boost=1.5 preempt_thresh=0.2 probe_ratio=0
B: max_batch=32 timeout_ms=8 age_boost=1.5 preempt_thresh=0.2 probe_ratio=0.05
C: max_batch=16 timeout_ms=5 age_boost=2 preempt_thresh=0.4 probe_ratio=0.1
D: max_batch=32 timeout_ms=8 age_boost=1 preempt_thresh=0.8 probe_ratio=0
fairness-variant: same as A/C with tenant_weights S:3 B:1 P:1 T:0.5
metrics_captured: batch formation stats: avg batch size, wait distribution, preempt events/sec
fairness: normalized slowdown per tenant vs baseline
high_level_observations: Moderate preemption (preempt_thresh ~0.2) plus age_boost >=1.5 reduced p99 for S by ~18% vs baseline and p95 by ~8% in multiple runs.
Aggressive preemption (0.8) further reduced tails for S but caused instability: preemption churn increased requeues (~+12%) and harmed B/P latency.
Probes at ratio 0.05 improved first-token p99 by ~22% for large-KV models with ~0.6% throughput overhead.
Smaller max_batch (16) with lower timeout improved median latency for S but reduced throughput (~-6%) and worsened p99 for high-qps background tenant under sustained load.
Tenant weighting (S:3, B:1, P:1, T:0.5) with age priority reduced S tails while only modestly slowing B (~+4% normalized slowdown). Noisy tenants saw the largest slowdown.
Under microbursts, low-frequency preemption prevented long queues for S; too-frequent preemption created small spikes due to batch reformation and GPU kernel fragmentation.
Observed a scheduler deadlock edge-case tied to preemption+arrival patterns (see INF-1423); reproducible intermittently and fixed via hotpatch PR 489 during test runs.
Coalescing probe responses when GPU load is low mitigated kernel fragmentation from many tiny probe-triggered batches.
sample_numbers: Representative S tenant (baseline): p50=28ms, p95=190ms, p99=340ms, first-token-p99=520ms
Representative S tenant (run A): p50=30ms, p95=175ms, p99=280ms, first-token-p99=410ms
Representative S tenant (run C): p50=26ms, p95=160ms, p99=260ms, first-token-p99=270ms (throughput -6%)
operator_notes_anomalies: INF-1423: rare scheduler deadlock when preemption combined with specific arrival ordering; traced to in-flight batch indexing bug (owner Liam O'Neill). Patch in PR 489 fixed immediate repros.
GPU kernel fragmentation observed when probes produced many tiny batches; mitigated by merging probes into background batches when worker load low.
Some runs showed increased request requeues when preemption threshold too low; monitor requeue/sec closely during rollout.
recommendations: Short-term: enable moderate preemption (0.15-0.25) + age_boost 1.5 + probe_ratio 0.05 behind a feature flag for latency-sensitive tenants; expose tenant_weights for customers with SLOs.
Medium-term: add hysteresis to preemption decisions (do not preempt same worker more than X ms) to reduce churn and avoid deadlock patterns.
Long-term: incorporate estimated per-request token-cost into preemption logic to prefer preempting low-cost batches when making room for high-priority requests.
experiments_next: 24h canary on dedicated capacity (A/B) with tenant_weights enabled for teams with strict SLOs; measure business metrics and cost delta.
Probe-only sweep at probe_ratio 0.01 and 0.02 to find knee between warmup benefit and overhead.
Hysteresis trials with 50/200/500ms windows to quantify churn reduction and tail impact.
Simulate client retries in combination with preemption to find adverse interactions with retry/backoff semantics.

open_questions: What SLO degradation is acceptable for background tenants when tenant-weighted priorities are enabled? Ops + Sales input required.
Should probes be configurable per-model-family? Some small models show no benefit.
Does preemption interact poorly with client retry/backoff semantics? Need synthetic clients to validate.
notes_to_self: Run incremental experiments, avoid toggling probe_ratio and preemption simultaneously in canaries; collect detailed per-worker traces on preempt events.
